newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MTBE prices softer, but still firm,.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MTBE prices softer, but still firm,.

text.p: Spot MTBE prices were slightly down but still strong in quiet trade on Monday amid talk that a tight pool of supply may find relief from imports next month.
Plants previously down for turnaround or technical problems are also coming back on stream, adding barrels to extremely low storage levels.
Players said trade was quiet on Monday, with the last deal heard done on Friday in the New York Harbor at 102.50 cents.
Sellers were pegged at 103.00 cents on Monday, about a half cent below Friday afternoon.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, spot MTBE was 0.50 cent lower at 96.00/97.00 cents. Any August barrels were about a half cent weaker at 95.50/96.50 cents.
"If you have barrels available in the beginning of August they are still very precious. But they get backwardated about after the 15th," said an MTBE trader.

Players said they were expecting shipments from Arco Chemical's 20,000 bpd plant in Rotterdam to finally begin arriving in the U.S. in mid-August. The plant, which had been down on turnaround, is a large exporter to the U.S.

On Monday, Superoctanos said its 12,500 bpd plant in Venezuela returned online on Saturday and is running at about 60 to 70 percent capacity. The facility, which had been down due to extended turnaround and other technical problems, is expected to be at full capacity by Wednesday.

In addition, Belvieu Environmental Fuels's 15,000 bpd plant has recently come back up after cutting short a turnaround that began on July 8 to take advantage of the high prices for MTBE, according to traders.
MTBE has risen more than 20 cents in the past month and the continuing wide spread between reformulated and conventional makes it an economical blending component for gasoline blenders.
